description: A clock with a master output and three more, each divided down from or multiplied up from the master tempo

params.text: Starts and stops the clock; it comes up running
Sets the tempo, 15 to 300 BPM, starting at 120; the display shows whatever tempo is in use
Sets this output's speed against the master, from a forty-eighth of it to forty-eight times it in 23 steps

inputs.text: A rising edge sets every phase back to the start
Any change from 0V starts the clock if it is stopped and stops it if it is running
Sets the tempo from outside: as a voltage doubling the tempo per volt with 0V for 120 BPM, or as a stream of clock pulses at the rate chosen on the menu

outputs.text: Carries a 1ms pulse at 10V at the master tempo, and 0V while the clock is stopped
Carries a 1ms pulse at 10V at its own divided or multiplied tempo, and 0V while the clock is stopped

notes: the three division settings are /48, /32, /24, /16, /12, /8, /6, /5, /4, /3, /2, x1, x2, x3, x4, x5, x6, x8, x12, x16, x24, x32 and x48, and each is shown beside its own output
in any of the pulse-counting modes an incoming pulse starts the clock by itself, and the clock stops again if no pulse arrives for a second
the maker's own note is that the external sync drifts at high speeds and needs a reset after a tempo change
menu: External Clock Mode — chooses how the external clock jack is read: as an Impromptu-style tempo voltage, or as 2, 4, 8, 12 or 24 pulses to the quarter note

inputs.0: high above 1V · stepped · one channel only
